module_title: The Reactivity Series and Metallurgy (Ores & Extraction)
introduction: Metals do not usually exist in their pure form in the Earth's crust; they are mixed with soil and other elements. The scientific process of extracting pure metals from their ores is called 'Metallurgy'.

core_concepts.title: Minerals vs. Ores
core_concepts.description:
1. Minerals: The naturally occurring elements or compounds in the Earth's crust. 
2. Ores: Minerals from which a metal can be extracted 'profitably and easily'. (Note: All ores are minerals, but not all minerals are ores).

core_concepts.title: The Reactivity Series
core_concepts.description:
Arranging metals in decreasing order of their reactivities. 
- High Reactivity: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al (Extracted via 'Electrolysis'). 
- Medium Reactivity: Zn, Fe, Pb, Cu (Extracted via 'Reduction' using Carbon). 
- Low Reactivity: Ag, Au, Pt (Found in the 'Free/Native state' in nature).

core_concepts.title: Roasting vs. Calcination
core_concepts.description:
1. Roasting: Heating 'Sulfide ores' strongly in the PRESENCE of excess air to convert them into oxides (e.g., Zinc Blende - ZnS). 
2. Calcination: Heating 'Carbonate ores' strongly in the ABSENCE/limited supply of air to convert them into oxides (e.g., Zinc Carbonate - ZnCO3).

core_concepts.title: Important Ores (Memorize for Matching Questions)
core_concepts.description:
1. Aluminum (Al): Bauxite ($Al_2O_3 \cdot 2H_2O$) 
2. Iron (Fe): Hematite ($Fe_2O_3$), Magnetite. 
3. Mercury (Hg): Cinnabar ($HgS$) 
4. Lead (Pb): Galena ($PbS$) 
5. Uranium (U): Pitchblende

important_entities.name: The Thermite Reaction
important_entities.significance: The reaction of Iron oxide ($Fe_2O_3$) with Aluminum (Al) is highly 'exothermic'. It releases so much heat that the iron is produced in a 'molten state'. This reaction is widely used to join (weld) cracked railway tracks and broken machine parts.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Remember this logic: 'Sulfide' (S) ores need oxygen from the air to become oxides, so they need air (Roasting). 'Carbonate' ($CO_3$) ores already have oxygen in them, so they don't need air (Calcination).

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite matching question in State PCS: 'Cinnabar is the ore of which metal?' Answer: Mercury.
